answer: A market town stays honest when every new identity must exhibit a distinct prize orchard harvest at a different county fair, judged live by a distinct panel that tastes the fruit and awards a single pearl to the winner. The first fake costs one fair, the tenth ten, and the twentieth twenty, so twenty invented agents would owe 210 fair entries. Bulk farming fails because each county holds one fair a year, judges are few, and one grower cannot stand at twenty judging tables on the same harvest day, like a pigment ground from berries that yields one true shade per batch.
